messages:
kat: heads-up — saw a surge of small GPU pods stuck Pending in us-west2-b for ~30m, started after the autoscaler burst. lots of tiny 0.25/0.5-GPU jobs piling up.
kevin: ugh that sounds like fragmentation. do we have node labels or taints that changed recently in that AZ?
maria: nothing changed on infra config, but noticeable spot evictions spiked in us-west2-b around 09:12 UTC.
kat: logs from scheduler show a bunch of ScorePlugin low scores due to 'shape mismatch' + topologicalSpread failures. snippet:
```
I0319 09:13:04.123456 1 scheduler.go:512] pod default/job-abc cannot be scheduled: node(s) didn't match pod affinity/anti-affinity
I0319 09:13:04.123458 1 scheduler.go:514] pod default/job-abc preemption needed but no victim found
```
sri: i pulled `kubectl get pods -n default -o wide` for a sample, lots of small gpu requests pinned to different instance types (p4d, p3dn, p3) which fragments packing. output:
```
NAME          READY STATUS   NODE           NODE-POOL   GPU
job-abc       0/1   Pending   <none>         p4-pool     0.25
job-def       1/1   Running   gpu-node-21    p3-pool     1
job-ghi       0/1   Pending   <none>         p3dn-pool   0.5
```
kevin: mixing instance shapes + strict topology spread is the killer. autoscaler ramped up heterogeneous pools. we need either a tiny-pod co-scheduler or enforce binpack by gpu type.
maria: also seeing increased cross-AZ bandwidth for some gRPC workers — network tail latencies spike when small pods land on remote racks, so preferring same-rack would help latency.
kat: proposal: 1) introduce a transient "tiny-pod" soft-affinity scoring class that prefers same-pool packing for <0.5 GPUs; 2) add a short-lived pod TTL binpack rebalance (evict/unschedule and reschedule within same AZ) for low-priority jobs; 3) canary the change in us-west2-b only.
sri: +1. for (2) we should bound evictions with a concurrency budget so we don't thrash. suggest budget=5 pods/min and backoff on network error.
kevin: I'll sketch scheduler-policy tweak: add a new Score plugin with weight 100 for same-instance-type, weight 40 for same-az, and set preemptionPolicy lower for tiny-pods. link to draft: https://git.internal/r/changes/PR-482
maria: what's the cost impact if we don't act? we had 14% more spot spills this week -> ~6% higher egress/cross-az tx and some retried runs. rough $$ estimate: $8k/month for that queue.
kat: ok sounds like action plan. @kevin can you open a roll-out PR with canary toggle + metrics (packing efficiency, avg pod pending time, eviction count)?
kevin: will do. i'll include dashboards: packing_util, small_pod_pending_90p, cross_az_tx. will set canary to 1 node pool first.
sre-bot: deploy-checklist: ensure chaos sims off for canary, add alerting if small_pod_pending > 50 for 5m and eviction_rate > 10/m.
sri: one more thing — add a sensor to autoscaler to avoid creating tiny heterogeneous nodes for that queue (pack tiny pods on older cheaper shapes instead of spinning new pools).
maria: good call. i'll coordinate with cost team to throttle pool provisioning for low-priority queues.
kat: thanks all. i'll monitor and will post updates here. if you see regressions ping me @kat. :eyes:
